Tencent.why: Hyperscaler cloud and foundation-model (Hy family) operator that buys AI compute at scale: Q2 2026 capex RMB52,784 million, primarily IT infrastructure (computer equipment, components) and data centres; cloud services revenue growth underpinned by demand for AI-related services.
Tencent.evidence: Results announcement 08-12-2026: 'At the infrastructure level, we substantially stepped up our procurement of compute' and 'Business Services revenue growth was primarily driven by increased revenues from our cloud services, underpinned by greater demand for AI-related services'.

players.product: Cloud services for AI-related demand, Hy family foundation models (Hy3) and in-house AI compute infrastructure (IT equipment and data-centre capex)

quarterly_data.quarter: Tencent press release: Announcement of the Results for the Three and Six Months (08-12-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Group results, Q2 2026 (company-wide): revenues RMB204.8 billion, up 11% year-on-year and 4% quarter-on-quarter; gross margin 58% (57% a year earlier), with higher depreciation and operating costs associated with expanded AI infrastructure offset by high-margin revenue streams; Non-IFRS operating profit RMB75.6 billion, up 9% year-on-year. H1 2026 revenues RMB401,243 million, up 10%.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 2026 revenues RMB204.8 billion (+11% YoY); gross margin 58%; Non-IFRS operating profit RMB75.6 billion (+9% YoY)

quarterly_data.quarter: Tencent press release: Announcement of the Results for the Three and Six Months (08-12-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Cloud: FinTech and Business Services revenues rose 9% year-on-year to RMB60.3 billion in Q2 2026; the company says Business Services revenue growth was primarily driven by increased revenues from its cloud services, underpinned by greater demand for AI-related services, ongoing international expansion and a more favourable pricing environment. Quarter-on-quarter the segment grew 0.7%, reflecting revenue growth in cloud services partly offset by seasonally lower commercial payment revenues.
quarterly_data.figure: FinTech and Business Services revenues RMB60.3 billion (+9% YoY, +0.7% QoQ); cloud revenue not separately disclosed

quarterly_data.quarter: Tencent press release: Announcement of the Results for the Three and Six Months (08-12-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: AI capex: capital expenditures were RMB52,784 million in Q2 2026, versus RMB31,936 million in Q1 2026 and RMB19,107 million in Q2 2025 (H1 2026 RMB84,720 million vs RMB46,583 million). Capex primarily consists of investments in IT infrastructure (including computer equipment, components and software), data centres, land use rights, office premises and intellectual properties. Capital expenditure payments in the quarter were RMB59.3 billion; property, plant and equipment rose to RMB198,909 million at 30 June 2026 from RMB149,905 million at 31 December 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 2026 capex RMB52,784 million (Q1 2026 RMB31,936 million; Q2 2025 RMB19,107 million); H1 2026 RMB84,720 million

quarterly_data.quarter: Tencent press release: Announcement of the Results for the Three and Six Months (08-12-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Company: 'At the infrastructure level, we substantially stepped up our procurement of compute, which will enable us to convert usage of our applications and models into revenue going forward.' Operating cash flow included large AI-related prepayments to provide infrastructure for Hy model enhancements, WorkBuddy and CodeBuddy inference needs, Weixin AI initiatives and AI capabilities across its products, as well as to meet growing external demand for its cloud services. Q2 2026 free cash flow was negative RMB13.8 billion (operating cash flow RMB52.7 billion against capex payments of RMB59.3 billion); excluding the prepayments for compute procurement, free cash flow would have been RMB37.6 billion. Net cash fell to RMB58.2 billion from RMB146.9 billion at 31 March 2026, primarily reflecting the capex payments and 2025 dividend payments.
quarterly_data.figure: free cash flow negative RMB13.8 billion in Q2 2026; RMB37.6 billion excluding compute-procurement prepayments

quarterly_data.quarter: Tencent press release: Announcement of the Results for the Three and Six Months (08-12-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: AI infrastructure running costs: technical infrastructure operations costs (excluding depreciation) were RMB15,212 million in Q2 2026 versus RMB7,546 million in Q2 2025, and depreciation of property, plant and equipment, investment properties and right-of-use assets was RMB11,161 million versus RMB7,651 million. R&D expenses were approximately RMB27,278 million (Q2 2025: RMB20,251 million); general and administrative expenses rose 22% year-on-year to RMB38.7 billion, primarily reflecting higher R&D spending to support Hy model enhancements, Weixin AI initiatives and AI capabilities across its products.
quarterly_data.figure: technical infrastructure operations costs RMB15,212 million (vs RMB7,546 million); R&D approximately RMB27,278 million (vs RMB20,251 million)

quarterly_data.quarter: Tencent press release: Announcement of the Results for the Three and Six Months (08-12-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Hy models: Tencent released the full Hy3 production version in July 2026, which it says delivered a substantial step-up in performance versus the Hy3 preview version and significantly outperforms most similar-sized models; the company says Hy3 has consistently ranked among the top 3 models globally by token consumption on OpenRouter since 7 July 2026, and describes Hy3 as a stepping-stone toward the Hy family attaining state-of-the-art capabilities in the future.

quarterly_data.quarter: Tencent press release: Announcement of the Results for the Three and Six Months (08-12-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: AI products: new AI products (primarily Hy, Yuanbao, CodeBuddy, WorkBuddy and Xiaowei) weigh on profit - Non-IFRS operating profit excluding new AI products contributions increased 19% year-on-year to RMB86.1 billion, versus RMB75.6 billion (+9%) including them. The company says its WorkBuddy AI office productivity service and CodeBuddy AI coding tool are achieving breakout user growth and are 'the clear leaders in their fields in China today' (company claim citing Analysys), with high user willingness to pay for tokens via subscriptions and top-ups; it has begun a small-scale prototype test of Xiaowei, the agentic AI inside Weixin, powered by a customised model, WeLM.
quarterly_data.figure: Non-IFRS operating profit excluding new AI products RMB86.1 billion (+19% YoY) vs RMB75.6 billion reported Non-IFRS
